modifications: Redacted a Mailgun-published EXAMPLE value: the placeholder HTTP signing key in the two regenerate-signing-key response examples was replaced with 'key-REDACTED-EXAMPLE-SECRET'. Documentation sample data (a fake key- prefixed value), not a real credential; GitHub secret scanning blocks the Mailgun key pattern. No path, operation, or schema is changed.
notes: Complete, verbatim copy of Mailgun's official 'send' OpenAPI 3.1 document (the primary Mailgun API spec): messages, domains, events, stats, mailing lists, routes, webhooks, templates, etc. openapi.json is the upstream YAML rendered losslessly to JSON. Mailgun publishes email validation as a separate OpenAPI 3.1 document (the Validations Service: single and bulk validation, list health previews, parse, thresholds) on the same hosts with the same basic auth; it is committed verbatim as upstream-validate.yaml (upstream.parts) and merged into openapi.json on every derivation, adding 26 operations. mailgun.js, the client the adaptor sets up on state.client, calls these (client.validate.*), so without them the spec was not the full API the adaptor reaches. Mailgun Optimize (InboxReady) and Inspect are separate products with their own credentials and are not included. MODIFICATION (overcommunicated): the published spec ships an EXAMPLE HTTP signing key placeholder that trips GitHub secret scanning; that one example value was replaced with 'key-REDACTED-EXAMPLE-SECRET' in upstream.yaml and openapi.json. It was documentation sample data, not a real credential; no path, operation, or schema is changed.
